lines: This plan covers 4 days, starting today.
The plan sets 1 cooking sessions: Thursday.
You cook on Thursday: the plan sets its sessions on those days, and nowhere else.
You planned 2 shops; the plan organises 1, one per cooking session — nobody shops more often than they cook. You can still go back for fresh food.
Shopping and cooking first thing in the morning, so it is ready by lunch.
For today, breakfast is off the plan: the day is already under way.
For today, lunch is not in the plan: there has to be time to shop first.
One shop, on Thursday: everything this plan asks for keeps until it is cooked.
To stay inside it, expensive proteins give first, then out-of-season produce, then variety — never the portions.
The Thursday cooking window is used for four overlapping batches, because the kitchen only allows one cooking day and later portions are frozen rather than held for too long.
Fresh noodles, rice and pasta are cooked at mealtimes, keeping their texture better than storing them in the Thursday batch.
